principles: Canonical/generated source text remains read-only; Korean text is a presentation-layer translation.
Preserve explicit subject distinctions: 士兵=병사, 部队=부대, 英雄=영웅. Do not insert a subject when the Chinese source omits it unless Korean grammar requires it without changing scope.
Preserve condition order, effect order, numerical values, percentages, plus signs, and duration exactly.
Preserve inequality semantics exactly: 高于/大于=초과, 低于/小于=미만, 大于等于/不低于=이상, 小于等于/不高于=이하.
Keep <color=#DC143C>...</color> markup attached to the same numeric value and preserve meaningful line breaks.
Use concise Korean game-UI wording; prefer 증가/감소/회복/발동 over explanatory paraphrase.
Named effects and skill-specific proper nouns are not auto-translated by the core dictionary; they enter the review queue.

statListStyle.note: 和/与 connecting two stats is rendered as 및; longer stat lists use commas.

reviewQueueRules: Text inside 「」 or other named-effect labels is reviewed separately instead of being translated by generic word replacement.
Skill-specific proper nouns and named mechanics such as 灼烧, 倒刺, 亡者苏生, 炼狱魔核 require individual Korean naming review.
Mechanics whose official Korean wording can materially affect interpretation, including 致命一击 and 近战伤害减免, require per-record review.
Unusual generation/revival wording such as 获得N个士兵 or 士兵全部阵亡 requires sentence-level review even when its component terms are fixed.
Reflection or damage percentages reused as a separate recovery percentage require sentence-level mechanic review.
